mission.hypothesis: A function-local GCC target("popcnt") setting should let the compiler use the hardware POPCNT instruction for each dependent update without changing global flags. The recurrence remains serial and ordered, and uint32_t addition preserves wraparound. The provided baseline uses a naive bit loop, so its measurement alone will not isolate target-local POPCNT against an unannotated builtin; that comparison needs a separately measured builtin candidate.

retained: Replaced the naive bit-count loop with __builtin_popcount in a helper compiled with GCC's target("popcnt") attribute.
Applied the same target attribute to run so the helper can be inlined into the recurrence without changing global compiler flags.
Preserved the nested loop order, uint32_t accumulation, output overwrite, and unused thread budget.

observations.claim: Le trial SWAR est valide et correct; sa moyenne mesurée est 0,00043538685 s (score 0,7061), contre 0,00104608787 s (score 0,5) pour le baseline. Ce sont les mesures affichées, pas une confirmation indépendante.

Le journal de correction rapporte six cas réussis (n=1, 17 et 1000; graines 23 et 60), sans erreur, avec entrées inchangées et gardes valides. Cela ne constitue pas une vérification exhaustive des 2^32 valeurs uint32.

uncertainties: Aucune mesure de confirmation indépendante n’est visible.

contract.statement:
Optimize the supplied baseline on AMD EPYC 9654 with GCC 14.2. Use the actual AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy.
For each pass j from 0 to parameter-1 and element i from 0 to n-1, update uint32 result += popcount(uint32(input1[i]) XOR result), starting at zero. Preserve unsigned 32-bit wraparound and this loop-carried dependency. Write one uint32. Benchmark n=1000, parameter=100, one core.
Edit only src/candidate.cpp. Keep extern C void run(const void*input1,const void*input2,void*output,int n,int parameter,int threads). Respect the threads argument as the CPU thread budget. Inputs are read-only and 64-byte aligned. Overwrite the full specified output on every call; no cached answers, external tools or libraries, filesystem, environment inspection, timing inspection or phase detection. Ordinary C++17, OpenMP and x86 intrinsics are available. Do not modify the protected correctness or timing protocol. Scratch allocation inside run is allowed and included in timing. The harness measures native wall-clock time, excluding input generation, oracle and compilation. Search and confirmation use different seeds. Numerical tolerances are fixed. The optimized reference source is withheld. Choose topics independently, record failed attempts, complete memory integration and independently confirm final G.
